newsitem.title: FRANCE: Keidanren sees 3 pct growth this year in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Keidanren sees 3 pct growth this year in Japan.

text.p: Keidanren Chairman Shoichiro Toyoda said on Friday that the Japanese economy would grow around three percent during 1996.
Toyoda, who is also chairman of Toyota Motor Corp, made the remarks at a luncheon for a Keidanren delegation in Paris hosted by the French employers' association CNPF.

Toyoda said Japan's gross national product shrank in the second quarter after surging more than 12 percent in the first, due to special factors. "For all of 1996, we think growth will be three percent," he told the luncheon in a speech that was translated simultaneously.
He said there were "signs of improvement" in the Japanese economy, with indications that the recovery, while still weak, was spreading to the non-manufacturing and small business sectors.
He urged fiscal and structural reforms to inject vigour into the recovery, and said Japan must encourage and nurture creativity for long-term economic advancement.
Toyoda also spoke of the need to raise venture capital for new ventures to encourage the development of new technologies which will provide the jobs of the future.
